name: Peripheral Daisy Obstructions
definition: Choose disjoint finite sets $P,R$ with $P\ne\varnothing$, a down-set $\mathcal W\subseteq2^R$, and a set $A\subseteq R$ such that $A$ and $R\setminus A$ are distinct inclusion-maximal members of $\mathcal W$. Form $O(P,R,A;\mathcal W)=(2^P\times\mathcal W)\setminus\{(P,A),(\varnothing,R\setminus A)\}$.
parameters: The displayed tuple must satisfy the down-set, nonempty cube-factor, complementary-maximal-pair, and irredundancy conditions in the coordinate normal-form theorem.
canonical_form: Every daisy obstruction with a peripheral coordinate has this form. Once a peripheral coordinate and reduced roots are fixed, the parameters are uniquely recoverable; distinct presentations may still describe isomorphic graphs.
recognition: A certificate gives $(P,R,A,\mathcal W)$ and verifies downward closure, complementary inclusion-maximality, and the two deleted vertices. Equivalently, delete a suitably maximal ambient-antipodal pair from a daisy cube with at least two roots.
comments: The single-root factor $\mathcal W$ may vary; this is a complete generative family rather than a finite list.
